protected_rule: DEC-157 (4): the fixed terms (grades and scales, the five gaps, origins, the queue's kinds, the path, the acts' names), the weights, every warning and dialog before an outward, signed or irreversible act, the court notice, and every "who can see this" notice. A protected word changed from the assistant's draft, or typed without one, shows only after a second check.
for_builders: A sentence on a screen that carries its data (a name, a count, a date) is keyed when the screen is built: screen.<id>.<part>, with {placeholders}; it is protected when it is a warning or dialog before an outward, signed or irreversible act, the court notice ("What a court can reach"), or says who can see something.

Reversible: you can undo this.
Reasoned: asks for your reason, which becomes part of the record.
Terminal: ends or removes something; reopening it takes a reason.
Signed: signed with your key, and stands under your name.
Irreversible: can never be undone.
The dots show how much the act weighs, from one to five.
Capture
how easily someone else could check that this copy is what its source published, unaltered
Connection
how easily someone else could check this link: that this payment, vote, office or person is the one meant
Testimony
how easily someone else could check what a witness says
Subject match
how easily someone else could check that this record is about this person or thing
A is easiest to check; D rests on a person's word. A grade never says whether something is true.
Undetermined
Undetermined: the record can't determine this from what your group holds, and the reason is always given. An answer, not an error.
Withheld
Withheld: something is here that you can't see, kept back by its source or by who may see it. That it exists is shown, never hidden.
Unrated
Unrated: not graded yet.
Nobody looked
Nobody looked: no one has searched for this yet. Not the same as “looked for, not found”.
Refused
Refused: Civicsmith won't do this. The reason says why, and what you can do instead.
Machine work
Machine work: made by the assistant or an automatic check, never by a member. It counts only once a member accepts it.
Another group's
Another group's: from another group's published case, recreated here. It counts only once your group accepts it.
Not yet evaluated
Not yet evaluated: no one in your group has judged this yet.
Accepted by our group
Accepted by our group: a member accepted it, with a reason you can open.
Flagged
Flagged: someone marked this for a second look.
Found by search
Found by search: Civicsmith matched these words in what your group holds. Nothing is recorded: a member records it, from its passage, with the usual act.
To do
To do: something only you can move forward.
Noticed
Noticed: something changed that you may want to know. Nothing is required of you.
Status
Status: where something you follow stands.
Working: not public; seen by your group's members.
Shared for review: named outsiders can read this draft until the owner stops sharing it.
Published: signed and public. It can be corrected by a new edition, never removed.
An answer is only as strong as the weakest thing it depends on: its weakest document copy and its least certain link, side by side, never merged.
A due date, counted on your group's local day. Open it to see the law or commitment it comes from and how the days were counted.
Hint · machine work: something the machine marked worth a look, with how it was found and out of how many. A lead, never a finding.
Hunch: a member's suspicion, labeled as one. Never evidence, and it never moves a finding.
Outward: this leaves your group's Civicsmith. Someone outside will see it.
Where you are: this band says who can see what you are working on.
Protected word: it protects members, so a change to it needs a second check before it shows.
Local name: the official name stays as it is, with an explanation in the member's language beside it.

What we look into
Our group looks into whether a government, an agency or a public body keeps its own rules and promises. We check what it says against its own records, and publish what the records show.
Every finding shows its source

Each finding we publish points to the passage it rests on: a page of a budget, a line of the minutes, a row of an office's own data. Open any finding in a published case and the passage opens with it, so you can read it yourself.
How strong the evidence is

Each piece of evidence carries a letter, A strongest to D weakest, and says why it has that letter: a copy fetched from the office's own website holds up better than one found elsewhere. A finding is never stronger than its weakest piece, and where something isn't known, the case says so instead of guessing.
What we publish, and who stands behind it
A case is published only when a member signs it. Once published it is never changed quietly: a correction comes as a new edition, and the earlier one stays readable with the correction beside it.
Have something for us?
Anyone can hand us documents or a tip without an account. The page says what will happen to what you give, and you decide how much to tell us about yourself.

Members join by an invitation from one of our administrators. If you would like to take part, ask a member you know, or tell us through “Have something for us?”. Members sign in from our page.

How members reach the assistant

The assistant is an optional helper, built on Anthropic's Claude. A member can ask it in plain words to find, read, answer or check things in what your group holds; it can suggest questions and documents, and draft translations. It answers only from what your group holds, gives legal information but never legal advice, and never concludes, signs or sends anything. What it does is labeled as the assistant's. Everything in Civicsmith also works without it.

words.en: The group's API key. One Anthropic API key, held by your group, serves every member who has no account of their own. Anthropic bills the key's owner for each use, so your group pays. It is off until an administrator switches it on. Each member is told once, before their first question under it, that their questions and the material read to answer them go to Anthropic under the group's account. Administrators see the key's use summed over members, never who used it or what was asked, and set the daily limit and whether the assistant may make suggestions unprompted.

Your group's Civicsmith keeps unpublished work from the public and from the people you look into, but a court order your group cannot defeat can still require anything not public to be shown: members' notes, sources, hidden projects. Some work is unlikely ever to draw such an order; journalists, lawyers and auditors may have protections others lack, such as shield laws or privilege. A group doing work that could draw one should make sure its members understand the risk.

What a spot-check does

A calculation counts what a source records, such as the reports the city marked closed. A spot-check tests whether the record matches what is really there: members visit a random sample of the counted items and record what they find.
Why the sample is random, and recorded

Civicsmith draws the sample from a recorded seed. Anyone, including the city or a reporter, can repeat the draw and get exactly the same items, so no one could have picked the easy or the damning ones.
words.note: adopted from screens-investigate's own rows; DEC-257: reworded

words.en: What the result says

The share of visited items that matched, and an exact range for the whole set. The range is what the sample can honestly support: the true share for all items is very likely inside it. A larger sample gives a narrower range: about 13 points either way for 40 items, about 9 for 100.
What it does not say

Nothing certain about any one item no one visited. Nothing about items outside the set that was drawn from. Items members could not judge are counted apart and named, never guessed; the estimate assumes they are like the rest, and says so.
Each visit is evidence

Each visit is recorded as the testimony of the member who made it. A photo, where the member took one, lets others see what was there; the member's account counts with or without one. A finding resting on a spot-check shows the draw, every visit, and the range.

Work done in Civicsmith can matter. Checking whether officials and agencies keep their own rules can show money misspent, deadlines ignored or promises broken, and a published case can lead to a correction, an audit or a lawsuit. People and organizations a group looks into sometimes go to court to see the work behind it.
The explanation is always one tap away for every member. You choose whether members are also told when they join and the first time they record something not public.

Hold your government to its own word

Civicsmith is free software for a group of people who want to know whether their government is doing what it must: obeying the laws that bind it and the court decisions it is subject to, keeping the rules it set for itself and the promises it made.

The group gathers the records, works out what they show, and publishes what it finds in a form anyone can check. Neighborhood groups, newsrooms, professional associations and offices checking their own work all use it the same way.
Start a group's Civicsmith
See what groups have published
How a group uses it

Gather the records. Members collect the records that bear on the question, from wherever they were published: the city's minutes, budgets, contracts and letters; state and federal regulations and reports; court decisions; the press releases and filings of private firms. Civicsmith keeps each one exactly as its source published it, with where and when it came from. Together these are the group's record.
Ask a question. In the group’s own words: “{example}”

Weigh the evidence. Members mark the passages of the record that bear on the question. Civicsmith grades each passage by how easily a stranger could check it, from a copy fetched straight from the office down to one person's word.
Reach a finding. The group's answer to its question, resting on named evidence, with how strong that evidence is. A hunch is kept as a hunch; it never becomes a finding.
Publish a case. The findings, their evidence and their strength, published together and signed by a member of the group. Anyone can read it and check it without asking the group.
What a group gets
Its own copy of Civicsmith. Each group runs its own copy, in a Cloudflare account the group controls. Nobody else holds the group's work, the people who make Civicsmith included.
Findings anyone can check. Every finding points to the passages it rests on and says how strong that evidence is, so a reader never has to take the group's word for it.

Help for people who have never done this. A guide walks each common job step by step, from asking an office for a record to publishing a case. An AI assistant is optional: it answers only from what the group holds, says where it looked, and never concludes, signs or sends. Everything works without it.
Free software. Civicsmith costs nothing. The group pays Cloudflare $5 a month for the account its copy runs in.
What Civicsmith does not do
It takes no side on what policy should be. It asks only whether the government kept its word.
It gives legal information, never legal advice.
It publishes nothing a member has not signed, and it sends no email.
Open it as any reader does: each finding, its evidence and how strong it is, and a way to check the signature without asking the group.
Already a member of a group?
Your group's Civicsmith has its own address, and you sign in there, not here: civicsmith.org holds no accounts. Ask your group for its address, or find it on your group's own website.
Write to the people who make Civicsmith: {address}.

words.en: For a group that has decided to create its own copy. This page says what you need, who should hold what, what happens step by step, and what it costs. Reading it takes five minutes; the installer takes about twenty.
Is it right for your group?

It fits if your group wants to find out whether a government, agency or public body is keeping the laws, rules and promises that bind it, and to show what the records say in a way others can check. It does not fit a group that wants a place to post opinions, or one that needs a lawyer's advice: Civicsmith gives neither.

A Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan, $5 a month, with a payment method. Cloudflare is the company whose computers will run your group's copy. Open the account in your group's name, not a person's.
About twenty minutes at a computer.

Nothing else. No server, no company, no technical knowledge, and no Claude account: the assistant is optional, and members connect their own accounts later if they want it. The installer asks you two things and does the rest.
Decide first: who holds the Cloudflare account

Whoever can sign in to that account controls your group's Civicsmith. They can read everything in it, and they are the way back in if every administrator is ever locked out. Agree as a group on who that is, and add a second trusted person to the account, so it never depends on one person. The installer says this again at the moment it matters.
What happens, step by step

You choose a short name and your places. The short name is a fixed label in your group's addresses and beside every signature; it never changes. The places are the city, county and state whose rules apply to you. Places ready now: {places}. For each, Civicsmith already holds the local facts it works from: its offices, where its records are published, its deadlines and its holidays.
Cloudflare asks your permission, on its own page, to let the installer create your group's copy in your account.
The installer puts your group's Civicsmith in place and checks it. About ten minutes. If a step stops, the installer says why and what to do; a stop before setup has begun creates nothing.
You claim it. The installer shows you a one-time password; you use it once, choose your own password, and become the group's first administrator. More administrators can be added later.
You set it up. Your group's name, the languages its members use, and whether members may use the assistant. All of it can be changed later.
You invite members. Each gets a link you send yourself, by whatever means you trust; Civicsmith sends no email. Each member chooses the name their work will carry.

$5 a month to Cloudflare for the account. If members use the assistant, its use is paid to Anthropic by whoever connected the account that serves it, and the group can set limits. Nothing is paid to the people who make Civicsmith.

words.en: Dividing does not remove anything. Every leg this question rests on gets a home on one of the children, including any leg that cuts against you, and this question stays on the record as the divided parent, recording where each leg went. Each child names this parent and every sibling, and when a child is published it names them to its readers. If you mean to drop material rather than re-home it, remove the citation, with a reason, instead.
words.note: affordances' DIVIDE_PROMPT (R5), shown before a question is divided

words.en: Grouping says these reasons are enough on their own to carry your answer. Your answer's strength is then taken from the strongest group rather than from its weakest single reason, so your name and the time go on each group you make and stay there until that group's reasons change. Nothing is hidden: every reason stays visible under the group you put it in, and a published case carries each group and what it reached inside the signed bytes, so a reader can check whether they really were enough on their own. Leaving the reasons ungrouped is always available, and is read as no stronger than the weakest one.
words.note: affordances' GROUND_PROMPT (R5; DEC-32 clause 1), shown before reasons are grouped

words.en: What co-attestation answers: when did these bytes exist? It asks an independent timestamp authority to record that this capture's exact bytes existed no later than a fixed instant. What it does not answer: whether the document is TRUE, whether its source is authoritative, or how close it stands to the fact you are citing it for. A secondhand report that is co-attested is still a secondhand report. What it is worth: it strengthens a Grade {ceiling} capture toward evidentiary weight. It never reaches Grade {unreachable} — that needs a chain-of-custody web archive this surface cannot produce.

words.en: A service that shares by default is offered only with its private mode, which Civicsmith turns on and checks on every call; if it can't confirm private mode, nothing is sent.

Not offered, because they share what is sent to them: VirusTotal uploads, Jotti, Hybrid Analysis, and the public modes of ANY.RUN, Joe Sandbox and urlscan.io. A tool whose vendor does not say whether it shares what it is sent is not offered until it does. An address check never sends the full address to anyone new: only checks that send a scrambled fragment, or Cloudflare's own. A site known to be bad: the document is still captured, as high risk, opens only in the safe view, and the check's answer is noted on it.
Sending security counts elsewhere (a log service your organization uses) sends counts only, never who opened which file.

How {product} grades a finding (method {version}).

1. Two strengths, never one. A finding has a capture strength (how faithfully the documents it rests on were taken in) and a connection strength (how firmly they are tied to what the finding is about), with testimony (a member's own firsthand account) graded beside them. Each is worked out on its own, from the legs graded for it, and they are never combined into one figure. Grades run from A, the strongest, to D.

2. Which legs count. A leg counts only for the strength its grade names. A capture grade is never above what the record holds for that document; a testimony grade is always D. A leg with no grade, or one marked as a hunch, is listed and counts for nothing: it never lowers or raises a strength. A capture or testimony grade written on a leg to another question, or to another group's finding, has nothing to grade and is listed, not counted.

3. Questions resting on questions. A leg to another question contributes that question's own strengths, worked out the same way, up to six steps down. Past six steps, or where that question's strength is not known, the strength is stated as undetermined: unknown, not low.

4. Another group's work. A leg to a finding of another group's case that this group has accepted contributes the strengths that accepted edition published for that finding, never more, and nothing below it is followed. If that finding cannot be read, the strength is undetermined. Withdrawing the acceptance later changes no grade.

5. Sets of reasons. Legs the author did not sort into sets of reasons are all needed together, so they are only as strong as the weakest of them. A set of reasons is only as strong as the weakest leg in it. Where the author named several sets that each carry the finding on their own, the strongest set is what counts. The strength is then the weaker of the legs needed by every set and that strongest set.

6. When a strength is undetermined. A strength is undetermined only when something it needs is unknown: one of the legs every set needs, or every set at once. A set that is unknown beside a known one could only be stronger, and is named. A strength with no counted leg is unrated, and says it rests on nothing established.

7. Anonymous testimony and evidence. Testimony from a member credited only to the group or the project, and material from an unnamed source that such a member attests, counts only when something independent beside it bears it out; otherwise it is listed and counts for nothing. What bears it out is a counted leg on a document that shares no origin with it (not the same document, not the same capture, not the same web address) and is not itself credited anonymously; for anonymous testimony, also a member's testimony credited by cover name or real name, by another member, sharing no origin with it. Testimony or material credited by cover name or real name is graded as usual.
8. What is named. Each strength names the leg that sets it, and every leg that does not count, with the reason. It also states how many hunches it left out.

8. Calculations, held standards and obligations. A leg to a calculation counts for the capture strength only, at the weakest of its inputs' capture strengths, each no stronger than where it came from: a figure quoted from a document by that passage, a money figure by its own grade, a table by its source, another calculation by its own capture strength. The arithmetic of the recipe never weakens it. A value typed in with no captured source is testimony, D. A value another program computed is unknown until that program's agreement has been measured. The method is stated beside the grade and is not graded. A calculation whose result is not accepted, or an input that cannot be read, makes the strength undetermined.

9. A leg to a held standard counts for the capture strength only, no stronger than the record holds for the text of that standard at the version cited; if the record holds no text at that version, the strength is undetermined.

10. A leg to one occurrence of an obligation counts for the capture strength only, at the weaker of the text of the rule in force and the record of the date that started it. Whether it was met, late or overdue is stated beside the grade and never changes it. Where any part of how it was worked out is unknown, the strength is undetermined.

That request does not name a question this record holds and you can read. Making a citation more specific happens on a question's reading of its evidence, so it needs the question first.

That question has no reading of its evidence by that name. A citation is made more specific in a NEW reading taken from an existing one, so the reading it starts from has to be named exactly as the question holds it.
That reading has no piece of evidence at the position named. Pieces are counted from zero, in the order the reading lists them.

That piece of evidence has no part to point at more precisely. It either rests on another question, which has no pages or passages, or on a document this record holds no copy of — and a part of something nobody captured cannot be named.

Making a citation more specific is a member's own act, done in their name. A machine may PROPOSE passages that look relevant, and they are listed for you to choose from, but choosing which passage is on point is a judgment a person signs for.

That request does not say which part of the document the citation should point at. Name the part — a page, a region of a page, a cell, a paragraph or a slide — or choose one of the proposed passages by its content id.

The part named cannot be recorded as sent: it names a field this act does not take, a value that cannot be written into the record, a content id this record does not hold, or both a content id and a description of the same part. It is refused rather than guessed at, because a citation quietly re-read would not be the one you made.

The part named is not in the copy of the document this citation rests on. Pointing the citation at a different document, or at a later copy of the same one, is not making it more specific — it is moving it, and a citation is never moved except by its own separate act.

The part named is not inside what the citation already points at — it is the same part, a wider one, or a different place in the document. Making a citation more specific can only ever point it at LESS of the document than before; anything else would claim a precision nobody established.

The new reading needs a name of its own, one the question does not already use. The reading it starts from keeps its name and stays exactly as it was: changing an existing reading in place would move a citation somebody else may be relying on.

The new reading needs a short account of what changed and why — which citation now points at less of its document, and what makes that part the one that matters. That account is what a later reader has to go on.

Ratifying puts a finding into the published record under a member's signature, and the member whose key signed it has to be the one who does it. The credential that asked here is an assistant's: it can prepare the finding and lay out what will be signed, and it cannot carry the signature in for you. Sign in and ratify it yourself.

Ratifying a case commits the group's own assertions about it — its scope, its completeness, its position on the people it concerns — under a member's signature. The credential that asked here is an assistant's: it can assemble the case document, and it cannot be the one who commits it. Sign in and ratify it yourself.

Ratifying puts a finding into the published record under a member's signature, and it is delivered by that member signed in as themselves. The credential that asked here is one of the operator's access tokens for your group's Civicsmith, not a person: a valid signature does not change that, because the credential that carries it in decides when the record changes. Sign in as the member whose key signed it and ratify it there.

Ratifying a case commits the group's own assertions about it under a member's signature, and it is delivered by that member signed in as themselves. The credential that asked here is one of the operator's access tokens for your group's Civicsmith, not a person, and a valid signature does not change that. Sign in as the member whose key signed it and ratify it there.

This document is a member's own firsthand observation, recorded before the record stopped writing its author's name into the observation's own files. Publishing it would publish that name whatever level its author chose, so it is not published. Its author can record it again as a new observation, which names nobody in its files.

This finding rests, directly or through another finding, on a member's firsthand observation recorded before the record stopped writing its author's name into the observation's own files, so it is not published. Rest the finding on a newer observation of the same thing, or publish it without that observation in its basis.

A finding in this case rests, directly or through another finding, on a member's firsthand observation recorded before the record stopped writing its author's name into the observation's own files, so the case is not published: that name would be published whatever level its author chose. Rest the finding on a newer observation, or leave it out of this edition.

This case edition uses a member's firsthand observation, or material from an unnamed source a member attests, and that member has not yet chosen how they are credited, so it cannot be signed. Publishing it at any level would be choosing for them. Ask that member to choose, or prepare the edition without the finding that rests on it.
This case document states an attribution for an observation that its author's choices no longer give. Prepare the case document again so it states what the authors chose, then sign that.
This observation's words are published only beside a signed case that states whose they are, and no signed case does yet. Sign the case document that uses it first.

This case document records a conclusion its project no longer stands on: since the document was prepared, the project withdrew that conclusion or concluded again differently. Signing it would publish a conclusion nobody holds. Nothing was committed. Publish the case again from the project, so the document records what the project stands on now, and sign that.

A project's own document is not published. A project publishes through its cases: publish a case from the project, have an owner sign the case document, and then ratify the findings in it. Nothing was published.

A finding is published only as part of a case its project has ratified, and no ratified case holds this version of it. Publish it into a case from its project, have an owner of the project sign the case document first, and then ratify this finding at the version the case holds. Nothing was published.

This is published only as evidence for a case, and no finding in any ratified case rests on it. Cite it from a finding, publish that finding's case and have an owner of the project sign the case document; an owner of that project can then sign this. Nothing was published.
Some of these documents are contested: a contradiction touching each is not yet resolved, and contested material is never released in a batch. They are named. Nothing was released.

This edition rests on testimony, or on material from an unnamed source attested by a member, credited only to the group or the project, with no independent leg corroborating it. Such testimony or evidence counts as an anonymous tip and supports a finding only beside an independent corroborating leg. Each such member, observation and document is named. Corroborate the claim with an independent leg, ask the author or the attesting member to choose cover or name, or drop the finding that rests on it. Nothing was signed.
Publishing at a set time means checking again at that time everything checked now, and part of it cannot be read now. It is named. Nothing was signed. You can publish now, or try again later.
This edition was not published at its set time: a source it rests on changed since it was signed. It is named. Nothing was published. Prepare and sign the edition again to publish it.

This edition was not published at its set time: a member who signed it has declared or withdrawn a tie to someone the case names since signing, so their confirmation of no undeclared tie may no longer hold. Nothing was published. Prepare and sign the edition again to publish it.
This edition was not published at its set time: a hold on the case or its project changed since it was signed. It is named. Nothing was published. Prepare and sign the edition again to publish it.

This edition was not published at its set time: a check made when it was signed no longer passes, or could not be made. The reason is given. Nothing was published. Prepare and sign the edition again to publish it.

Moving documents from collected to verified is a decision a named person makes and signs. The credential that asked here is an automated one, so it can gather the batch and lay out the review, and cannot be the one who says the batch is good. Sign in and release it yourself.

Releasing a batch at once records your explicit acknowledgment that the batch is of a piece and that you weighed the risk of doing them together. Without it the record shows only that a button was pressed.
Releasing a batch at once records what you actually did to check it — what was sampled and what was verified. A concrete note can be audited by somebody later; silence cannot be audited at all.

This document claims to be part of a published case, and it does not carry what a part of a published case must carry, so it was not written. Each problem is named beside this message. Nothing in the record changed.

words.en: What a project is aiming at is a member's decision. An assistant may point out gaps; it may not set or change the measure. Sign in as a member. Nothing was written.

words.en: A comparison sets out rows and questions for members; it never states whether the act complied. Remove the outcome. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Take a proposal up as proposed, take it up edited, or write your own instead. Nothing was written.
words.note: hypotheses' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This proposal was already taken up or set aside. Nothing was written.
words.note: hypotheses' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This cites as yours a passage a machine proposed, and you have not taken that proposal up. Take it up first, as proposed, in your own words, or with your own reading instead; then you may cite it as yours. Nothing was changed.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A proposal of the system's says how it was worked out. Nothing was written.
words.note: hypotheses' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A proposal of the system's carries its measured false-alarm rate, a share between 0 and 1. Nothing was written.
words.note: hypotheses' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say why you are setting this proposal aside. Nothing was written.
words.note: hypotheses' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This service is held back until its vendor states how it handles the files it is sent. Nothing was added.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your group's Civicsmith does not offer this service, for the reason stated beside it. Nothing was added.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This tool would share the files it is sent with others, so your group's Civicsmith will not send it any. Nothing was added.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Part of the record this answer depends on cannot be read by your group's Civicsmith yet, so nothing is answered in its place. Nothing was written.
words.note: escalation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your group's Civicsmith knows no security service by that name, or the service needs an address that was not given. Nothing was added.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This group's Civicsmith offers no public read by that name. Nothing was changed.
words.note: public-read's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This goal is closed, or this aspiration is retired. It stays readable with everything recorded under it, and it does not reopen. Nothing was written.
words.note: intent's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An aspiration is held until it is retired, and a goal is open until it is closed. No other move is accepted, and neither comes back. Nothing was written.
words.note: intent's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A goal says what it pursues and what bounds it, and an aspiration says what it holds to. Something here is empty. Write it and send it again. Nothing was written.
words.note: intent's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The amount is kept exactly as the body wrote it, but it has to read as a number — digits, with an optional decimal part and thousands separators. Otherwise it cannot be set beside another quote.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A request is named by its position in the action's correspondence, which is a whole number counted from zero. Give that number to see only the quotes answering that request.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A quote answers a request, and this one names no earlier sent entry in this ledger. Record the request first, then name its position as the entry this quote answers.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A quote is what a body sent back, so it belongs on an entry recording something received. Record the reply as received and put the quote on it.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A quote records the currency the body named. The record will not assume one, so say which currency the amount was quoted in.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Quotes are listed by the body that quoted them or by the request they answer. Name one of the two — not neither, and not both at once.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A revision names the earlier quote it changes, and the position given holds no quote. Both the original and the revision stay on the record, so the revision has to point at a real one.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The currency or the stated basis is too long, or holds a quotation mark, a backslash or a line break, which the record cannot store. Shorten it or leave those characters out.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: No proposed passage or connection you can see goes by that name, so nothing was accepted.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reading of a response is one of: complied, partial, denied, or none (nothing came back in time). Nothing was written.
words.note: escalation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A determination records what was required, what was done, and why, and never what should be done. Propose an action instead. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The law a records request is made under is named by its citation, a short reference such as a code section, and only a records request carries one. This write stated a law that was too long to be a citation, was not text, or sat on a kind of action that is not a records request. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A recorded re-evaluation says what was looked at and what was decided. The note is missing, too long, or holds a quotation mark, a backslash or a line break, which the record cannot store.
words.note: reevaluation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing that finding rests on has moved in the way named, or the finding is not one you can read here, so there is no second look owed to record. Ask for the finding's re-evaluations to see what is owed.
words.note: reevaluation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A finding this case relies on rests on material your group's Civicsmith does not hold whole, and everything a case relies on travels with it in full. Find a presentable copy, stop relying on the material, or make the finding supporting. Nothing was written.
words.note: case-disclosures' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reminder is set on a deadline of the action that has a date, for a day written year-month-day; it changes or removes only a reminder of your own; it is not set twice on one day; and an action holds at most 50 reminders. This request did not meet one of those, so nothing was changed.
words.note: action-clocks' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This move says how the action ended while moving it somewhere that is not an ending. Recording an outcome the action has not reached would put a result in the record before there is one.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reading of none says nothing came back in time, so it names no reply. Nothing was written.
words.note: escalation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This vendor keeps some of the files it is sent for its own research. Confirm that you accept that before it is added. Nothing was added.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The group has retired this material, recording that it is superseded or no longer stands, so a citation made now would read to everyone after you as live support nobody will look at again. Cite whatever superseded it, or collect the source again as a new item and cite that. A document its publisher withdrew or changed is a different thing and can still be cited.
words.note: citation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This change says the item was made at a different time than the record holds. A change can alter what a document says, but not when it was made: the record orders its history by that date, and letting a later change move it would let anyone backdate something. Nothing was written. Send it again with the date the record holds, or with none.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This change says the item was produced by a different group than the record holds. A change can alter what a document says, but not whose it is: the record keeps who produced each thing so it can be held to account, and letting a later change move that would let anyone re-attribute it. Nothing was written. Send it again with the group the record holds, or with none.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This change would turn something the record already holds into a different kind of thing, an item of information into an action, say. A change can alter what a document says, but not what it is, because what it is decides which rules protect it. Nothing was written. To record it as the other kind, create a new one of that kind and link the two.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A proposed risk tier carries its basis: what the proposer read the tier from, in its own words, kept beside the proposal. The basis was missing, longer than 500 characters, or held a quotation mark, backslash or line break, which this record cannot store. Nothing was written, and the action's tier was never going to change.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This action's record of earlier risk tiers is not in a shape the act can add to without rewriting it, and the act only ever adds. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Changing a risk tier needs a reason, and it is kept beside the change for as long as the record lasts. The reason was missing, longer than 500 characters, or held a quotation mark, backslash or line break, which this record cannot store. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A risk tier is 1 (file freely), 2 (file with caution) or 3 (do not file without counsel), or it is left unstated, which reads as not assessed. This write stated something else, so nothing was written.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: After an action is created, its risk tier changes only through the risk-tier act, which records who changed it, when and why, and keeps every earlier tier readable. This write would have changed the tier, or the record of its earlier tiers, some other way, so nothing was written. Use the risk-tier act.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: What material does for an answer is a property of a question's basis, and the thing citing here is a case. A case's citation carries no such part, so this one would be dropped rather than recorded — and a field stated in one place and honored nowhere is how a record and the pages built from it drift apart.
words.note: citation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Each standard is compared in rows: what it requires, what was done, and whether the two align, diverge or are open. A standard has no row, or a row is missing a part. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record's rule services are switched off in your group's Civicsmith until the assistant's measured bar is met. Nothing was read.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A rule service of that name is already held; the first one stays. Nothing was changed.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: No rule service of that name is held in your group's Civicsmith. Nothing was read.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The investigation this names has ended, and an ended investigation reads and proposes nothing more: its work is read against the conditions it ran under, and those stopped when it stopped. Nothing was done.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The safe copy of this file could not be made. The tool's reason is stated beside it. The original is unchanged.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The safe copy of this file is being made. Ask again shortly.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The safe copy of this file has not been found clean by the file scanner, so it is not handed out. The safe view is still there.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The safe view of this file could not be made. The reason is stated beside it. The original is unchanged.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This file is high risk, so it opens as its safe view. A deeper check that passes opens the original to every member for a day, or you can open it after the warnings.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The safe view of this file is not made yet. It is made soon after a file is captured; ask again shortly.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: You already asked to release this hold. A second, different member has to agree before it is released.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The file scanner your group's Civicsmith uses did not answer, so nothing was scanned and no note was written. It is asked again on its next round.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A scanner reported a finding in this file, so its original is held and does not open. The safe view still opens, and the file keeps its place in the record. Two members can release the hold, each with a reason, or a second, different scanner can clear it in a deeper check.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This file is being scanned before it opens. Ask again in a moment; the safe view can be read meanwhile.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This high-risk file was last found clean more than a week ago, and the scanner cannot check it again now, so the original was not opened. Read the safe view, or ask for a deeper check.
words.note: file-safety's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A records request may name the stages it asks the records for: one to twelve different entries, each naming a progression, an entity and a stage in at most 200 characters each, and each stage one its progression declares. Only a records request names them. This write named them otherwise, so nothing was written.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A document acknowledged as self-attested only is either co-attested already or not one this case rests on, so it needs no acknowledgment. Remove it from the list. Nothing was written.
words.note: case-disclosures' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Publishing a document as self-attested only says why. Give the reason. Nothing was written.
words.note: case-disclosures' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The venue's reference for this sending is one line of 1 to 100 characters, as the venue gave it. Nothing was recorded.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Somebody already recorded a decision to cut this dependency, which is different from there never having been one. Citing it again would neither reverse that decision nor step around it, so putting the link back is a separate act that records its own reason.
words.note: citation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A determination records whether the act complied, not how much it matters. Significance, severity, priority, urgency, rank and score are members' judgments made with the consequences in front of them. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The owners have already been asked to sign this edition, and it is in their queues. Nothing was written. The answer shows who asked and when.
words.note: tasks' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This write names a history entry this document already has, and it is a different write from the one recorded there. The record never rewrites its history, so nothing was written. Send it again under a new history key.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This source of proposals is already registered. A source registers once, when your group's Civicsmith starts.
words.note: intent's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A source of proposals names its kind and gives a reader. This registration does not.
words.note: intent's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That stage does not belong to this kind of entry. A request, a fee-waiver request, an appeal or a court filing is something sent; an acknowledgment, a fee estimate, a decision, an extension notice, a production or a denial is something received. A non-response carries no stage.
words.note: action-grammar's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Actions are attached at notification, legal tools and political accountability. The escalation's stage now takes none. Nothing was written.
words.note: escalation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This standard does not bind this body, so the act cannot be found nonconforming against it. Record it as a benchmark comparison: below, slower than, or above. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A standard named was not in force when the act was done, by the period the record states for it. An act is measured against the standards that applied to it. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Name which side of the question states what the standard requires, a or b. Your group's Civicsmith never chooses it. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This standing question has ended, and an ended question is never started again. Set a new one if you want it to keep running. Nothing was changed.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A standing question needs an end date after today, so it does not run for ever. Nothing was written.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A standing question keeps one search: a saved search, or a find in a document, a set or a project. Give one of these, not both. Nothing was written.
words.note: answers' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That is not a move this item can make from where it stands. Each kind of thing has a set of moves its rules allow, and this one is not among them, so nothing was written. Move it by a step the rules allow, or leave it where it stands and record what changed.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This work is already an open step on the question. Use that step, or add your question to it. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A date for a step is a calendar day, with what sets it: the law, a meeting, or your own choice. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A cost is a fee or a purchase: an exact amount, its currency's three-letter code, and what it paid for. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A step ends as done (ended) or set aside, and only once it is planned or under way. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A proposed step is taken up as proposed, taken up with your own wording, or set aside for a step of your own. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An outcome is helped, a dead end, or not yet judged, recorded for a question the step is on. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A step is taken on one or more questions, in one project, or for the whole group: exactly one of these, and a step is never placed inside another step. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Name what the step produced by the record's own id: a record, a capture, a passage, a lead or a derived connection with its derivation. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reminder is set for a calendar day. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Write it in your own words, within the length it allows. Nothing was written, and nothing was cut.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A step waits on another step, on something arriving, or on a date. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A part of your group's Civicsmith tried to register something it had already registered, or that another part already provides, so the second registration was refused and the first still stands. This is a fault in how your group's Civicsmith was built, not in the record, and nothing in the record changed.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The system never judges whether a step helped or was a dead end; a member does. It ends its own step with every outcome not yet judged, or sets it aside with its reason. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Only a member does this, in their own words and by their own choice. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A part of your group's Civicsmith tried to add its own check to every promotion without naming itself, so nothing was registered. This is a fault in how your group's Civicsmith was built, not in the record, and nothing in the record changed.
words.note: promotion's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This step is a project's own, and a question's use of it would show it beyond that project. Take a step on the question instead. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A step is work done toward an answer, never part of what a finding rests on. Rest the finding on what the step found. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The system acts only on the steps it took itself. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The system takes a step only for a run it holds, and this credential holds no such run. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say what the work is, in your own words, in at most 500 characters. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This proposed step was already taken up or set aside. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A member takes a step themselves; a proposal is the system's or an assistant's. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: More than one question uses this step. Name the question whose use of it you are removing. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This names a step the work serves, and the step could not be read here, so nothing was tied to it. Nothing was proposed.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This step waits on something not yet met, named here. It starts once each wait is met or removed. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This wait would close a loop: the steps named would each wait on the other and none could start. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This step would wait on a step fewer people can see, so some who see it could not see what it waits on. Nothing was written.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Work was done on this step, so its record is kept. Set it aside instead. Nothing was deleted.
words.note: steps' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The text still holds a blank the record could not fill, marked UNFILLED. A member writes it in before the text can be approved.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A detector looks at money facts, contracts and patterns over facts, never at a person; this definition names a person. Nothing was defined.
words.note: money-checks' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A field this reading has to fill in carries filler text rather than an account of anything. A required field filled to get past a check is worse than an empty one, because it reads to the next member as something somebody wrote.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Two parts of this reading are offered as separate routes to the same answer, and the record can show they trace back to the same original material. Treating them as separate makes the answer look better supported than it is, so a machine may not put it forward that way; a member may still say they are genuinely separate, and that is their call to sign for.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record holds more material behind this question than could be checked in one pass, so whether this reading is genuinely new, or genuinely made of separate parts, was not settled either way. Not finishing the check is a different fact from passing it, and this record does not let the two read the same.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Reporting that a level of the search is empty means saying WHICH level was searched and where the log of that search can be read. Absence at one level is not absence at the next, and an unattributed empty answer is the one shape nobody can check.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: One of the pieces of evidence this reading rests on cannot be reached where it says it is: it is not in the record, it cannot be read from here, or the record has retired it. A reading resting on something retired reads to a later member as live support for the answer.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This question already holds a reading by that name. Names are unique within one question so a member can ask for a reading by name, and a second one wearing the same name would make every later reference ambiguous.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Only a question carries readings of its evidence, and the thing named here is not a question. There is nothing under it for a suggestion to be a reading of.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This reading of the evidence is the same in substance as one this question already holds, so it is not put forward a second time. The reading it matches is named, and adding a duplicate would grow the review pile without adding anything to review.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This question has no readable file behind it, so there is nothing for a reading of its evidence to be added to. That is a fact about the question rather than about the reading, and nothing was composed.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Every suggestion names the piece of work that produced it, and this one named none that can be read here. What was searched, under which declared conditions, and where it stopped is what lets anyone else check a reading rather than take it on trust.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That request did not say which question the suggestion is about. A reading of the evidence always belongs to one question, so it asks rather than guessing.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This suggestion is about a question the investigation was not working on. An investigation is read against its own question, or the questions its project draws on, so work on a different question starts an investigation of that question.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The strength of this reading does not work out over the structure it declares, on one or both of the two things strength is measured on. A reading whose arithmetic cannot be run is a reading nobody can check, and it is not put forward.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The investigation this suggestion names has ended. A suggestion is read against the conditions of the investigation that produced it, and those stopped being current when it stopped, so going on means starting a new one.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This suggestion rests on more pieces of evidence than one reading may carry. The limit is published in the refusal so a caller can split the reading rather than guess at what would have fitted.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A suggestion is one of five kinds and this one names none of them. The kinds are a closed set so that a run reporting an empty search is told apart from a run that reported nothing at all, which no other field can distinguish.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This question's own file could not be extended in place, so nothing was written. Adding a reading edits the record the reading lives in, and a half-written record is worse than an unchanged one.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This suggestion tries to arrive already decided — settled, set aside, hidden, or signed by somebody. A suggestion may only ever arrive as something put forward; deciding what to do with it is a named member's act and no automated caller can reach it.
words.note: run-productions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A determination supersedes only an earlier determination of the same act. The one named is about another act. Nothing was written.
words.note: conformance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This task is not yours to act on: it is with another member now, so nothing was done to it. The record says below who holds it. Ask them, or an administrator, if it still needs you.
words.note: tasks' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Name a template or write the words, not both.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A template is drafted from a draft a member has approved. Approve the draft first.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The template named is written for another kind of action. Name one written for this kind.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The jurisdiction profile holds no file template for this kind: name a template, or write the words.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The template named is a briefing to counsel: it serves a counsel packet, never a filing.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The template named is wording the group files in its own name: a counsel packet's briefing takes a brief template.
words.note: filings' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record could not be read completely for conflicts on this case's findings, so what must be disclosed is not known. Try again. Nothing was published.
words.note: case-disclosures' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A finding in this case rests on something the record holds in unresolved conflict, and a case may be published with it only if the conflict is disclosed. Each one is named. One in conflict with a record you cannot see is named by its finding, and the published case will highlight it without naming that record. Disclose it, or resolve it first. Nothing was published.

The record keeps what it looked for only when something can be named as the reason — an investigation, a monitoring sweep, a link in a document, a ratification, an acquisition, an extraction, a derivation, a lead somebody wrote down, a standing objective, or a step taken for a question. That observation says the thing is there without saying what was found. A record that something is present has to point at what it found — the captured document, the passage, the entity — or nobody can check it later, and a claim of coverage that cannot be checked is worse than no claim at all.

That observation says nobody looked, and an observation is the record of a look. Never having looked is what the record says of a subject with no observation at all, so it is not written as one. A look that happened records what it found: nothing, something, part of it, or that it could not tell.

words.en: An agent credential has to say who stands behind it: the organization as a whole, or one named member. The two carry different accountability and they see different things, so the record will not hold one that says neither.

words.en: Withdrawing an agent credential is recorded against the person who withdrew it, so a named member has to be the one doing it. An automated caller has no name to put there and the record would then show a decision nobody made.

words.en: There is no agent credential by that name in your group's Civicsmith, so nothing was withdrawn. Being told that plainly matters more than it looks: believing you have taken an authority away when you have not is the worse of the two outcomes.

The whole of what this act puts on the record is why you judged that the change in the lens does not bear on this work — without it the record would say only that somebody decided, and a later reader could not tell whether the question was answered or waved away. Say why, and it is settled.

words.en: Reading a policy proposes a bias set; it never adopts one. Adopting is something a member does with their name on it, because otherwise a group could say it follows an organization's standards without anybody in the group having agreed to anything.

words.en: A pattern statement is a claim about how an institution actually behaves, so it is analysis and needs evidence in the record. It can be written in draft without one; it cannot leave draft without one.

words.en: This bias set is adopted and does not say what it does NOT check. A case held to a standard has to say which parts of that standard this system verifies and which it does not — the parts that can be counted are rarely the parts that protect, and enforcing only the countable half while staying silent would carry the authority of the whole policy without its substance.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement assigns a truth value to a source wholesale, and declared bias may never issue verdicts. It may raise scrutiny, it may block an inference, and it may assert a pattern it can evidence. The construct that fights undeclared distortion is held to a higher standard than the distortion, so this is refused whoever declares it.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That is a standard of evidence — how strong support must be before you assert it — and a standard is a BAR rather than a lens. Declare it as your project's required strength, where it will actually refuse work that falls short. Filed here it would refuse nothing, because a declared bias is disclosed and never gates.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: One of these bias statements is missing something the record needs to apply it: a stable name, one of the three kinds it can be, or the sentence itself. The three kinds are raising scrutiny on a source, blocking or licensing an inference, and asserting an evidenced pattern — a standard of evidence is not one of them; that is a bar.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement does not say why the lens is held. A declared bias the system honors is one its author justified; without that it is an unstated prior with a form around it.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement names its subject in prose rather than pointing at the subject registry. Registry entries are what let the record notice when a project statement and a group statement are about the same thing — in prose, nothing can tell, and a collision that is quiet is the one this construct exists to prevent.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A phase starts after, or a judgment leads to, a phase of the same scenario, or a matter the plan is about. The one named is neither. Nothing was written.

words.en: A new measurement cannot re-grade the documents already read by that engine, and that holds even when the new measurement is WORSE. What the record does instead is name exactly which transcriptions were graded under the old measurement, so a person can look at them and decide. Grades in this record are things people put their name to.

words.en: Nothing here was actually measured. A release note, a changelog, a model card or a new version number all tell you an engine CHANGED — none of them tells you how well it now reads a page, and that is the number the record grades against. Run the probe and record what it scored, including the inputs you gave it, so somebody else can disagree with you later.

words.en: This measurement is not readable as one. It has to name an engine, a version, a date, and the probe run that produced it — and the quality figure, where there is one, has to be on the same scale the rest of this record uses.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This announcement carries a quality figure. Noticing that a vendor announced something is useful and the record keeps it — it brings the next check forward. But what they say about their own product is a claim, and a grade in this record rests on a measurement. The announcement cannot stand in for the check, and it cannot change a grade on its own.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This announcement is not readable as one. It has to say which engine it is about and where you saw it, because it is somebody else's statement about their own product and the record keeps it attributed to them.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: To put an engine on the calibration schedule you have to say which probe will check it. Registering measures nothing yet, but a schedule with no stated way of measuring is a promise nobody could keep, or tell was kept.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: To put an engine on the calibration schedule you have to say which engine. Registering it measures nothing yet — it only says what will be checked, and so it has to name it.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This measurement does not say who ran it. A measurement is something somebody did, and a later reader who doubts the figure needs to know whose it is to ask for it to be run again.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A measurement has to carry the day it was taken. How good an engine is, is a fact about a particular day — without one, nothing can tell whether anybody has checked recently, and nothing can ever supersede it.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A measurement has to say exactly what it measured — which engine, and which version of it. Services are retrained and re-released under the same name, so the name alone cannot tell a later reader whether the thing you measured is the thing that read their document.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This capture could not be recorded as belonging to anybody in particular, so it was not made. An act that names one party where two acted reads as though a person did something a machine did, or the other way round, and that is worse than a missing document.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The site this would fetch from has asked us to slow down, or has refused us recently, and we are waiting the interval it named. The request is still queued and will be made when the wait is over — nothing has been lost and nothing needs re-asking.

words.en: Every request your group's Civicsmith makes says what it is for, so a source can tell a first capture from a routine re-check and throttle one without blocking the other. This one names a purpose that is not one of the things it could truthfully be doing.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This round of fetching has already been to that site once. Requests are spread out rather than sent in a burst, so this one waits for the next round. It is still queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your group's Civicsmith will not fetch without saying who is asking and how to reach whoever is running it. Being refused honestly is a fact that can be recorded; being admitted by disguise is a claim that could not be defended later.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request asked to fetch as the member's own browser, and the record does not hold what that browser is. Presenting an agent nobody actually used would be inventing a client rather than speaking as one, so it asks rather than guessing.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your group's Civicsmith tried to fetch the document and the fetch did not land, so nothing was captured. That says nothing about the document or the site beyond this one attempt, and it is recorded as a look that could not tell. The request is still queued and is tried again on a later round, until it expires.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record already holds this document, under another record. A document has one home in the record — the first record that registered it — and registering it again here would move it away from there. Nothing was written.
