words.en: That matter is already in an open plan of this project, which is named. A matter is in one open plan of a project at a time; work in that one, or close it first. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That matter is no longer live: the determination has been superseded, or the question is closed. Plan from the live one. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A plan is about the project's own matters: a question the project draws on, or a determination the project made. This one belongs to another project. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This investigation has already opened as many questions as the member who started it allowed. Nothing was created. The investigation ends at its next step and says which limit stopped it.
words.note: run-rules' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This investigation was not given a limit on how many questions it may open, so it may open none: an assistant opening questions without a limit fills the record with questions nobody asked for. The limit is set by the member who starts the investigation. Nothing was created.
words.note: run-rules' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An assistant opens a question only inside an investigation it is running, and this one named none that can be read here. The investigation is what records the lens and the purpose the question was opened under, so without one nothing could say why it exists. Nothing was created.
words.note: run-rules' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The investigation this question was to be opened inside has ended. A question is read against the conditions of the investigation that opened it, and those stopped being current when it stopped. Nothing was created; a member can start a new investigation.
words.note: run-rules' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A target names what is measured and the passage stating it, a threshold (at least, at most or within, an exact number and its unit), the period it applies to, and the body's definition of the measure or that none is stated. The answer names the field not in that form. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This document is a member's own observation, and this revision no longer says so. Removing that would let a member's word read as a captured document. What the document is cannot be revised; to withdraw an observation, record a new one.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This document claims to be a member's own firsthand observation, but it did not come through the act that records one. Only that act can mark a document as an observation, because only that act takes the author from the signed-in account. Record the observation through it, or remove the claim.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That request names who the author is. The record takes the author of an observation from the account that is signed in, never from the request — a request that names its own author could sign as somebody else. Send the observation without an author and it is recorded as yours.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A firsthand observation is a person saying what they saw, in their own name, and it stands on that person's trust. The credential that asked is an automated one, and it has no eyes to have seen anything with. Sign in and record it yourself.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The observation is empty. Write what you saw, in your own words; nothing is filled in for you.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An observation needs the date you saw it, as a calendar date (for example 2026-09-10) or a date and time, and not a date later than now. The record keeps that date apart from the moment you wrote it down, because they are two different facts.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This document is a member's own observation, and this revision of its record claims it came from somewhere else — a fetch, a sweep, or a machine. That would let a member's word pass for a captured publication. An observation's origin is the member who made it, and that cannot be revised.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record already holds, under another document, the exact bytes this observation would be stored as — which can only happen if somebody registered them in advance. Nothing was recorded. Try again: the next attempt is stored under a new identifier and new bytes.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The observation is longer than one passage this record stores. Record it as more than one observation; each is kept exactly as written and each can be cited.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The text of a standard behind a paywall or in a reading room is held only from a capture a member made themselves. A passage named was captured another way. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A theme is declared by a person, in their own name, and every reading of it shows whose lens it is. The credential that asked is an automated one, which has nobody behind it to hold the idea. Sign in and declare it yourself.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That leg rests on a THEME. A theme is one member's declared lens — an idea they use to gather material — and it is never the basis of a claim, so nothing can rest on it or on a document's membership in it. Cite the document or the passage itself: what a finding rests on is content, whatever theme led you to it.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: No theme is recorded under that id. Use the id the declaration returned, or list the themes to find it.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A theme needs its idea in a few words — what you are calling it, such as "deferred maintenance" — as well as its test. Nothing was declared.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A proposal must say who proposed it, and this one arrived carrying nobody. The record stamps the proposer from the credential that asked; nothing was written.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A theme needs its TEST: one sentence a document or a passage either passes or fails, so any member can check a placement against it. Without one the theme is a label anything could wear, and it cannot be declared.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Placing a document in a theme is a member's judgment that it passes the theme's test, recorded in their name. An automated credential may only PROPOSE a placement, which stays a hunch until a member confirms it. Sign in to place it, or propose it instead.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The note on this placement is longer than the record stores in one passage. It was refused rather than cut. Shorten it and try again.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing you can see in the record answers to that document or passage id, so it cannot be placed in a theme. Name a document by its id, or a passage by the content id it was minted under.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The theme's name or its test is longer than the record stores in one passage. It was refused rather than cut, so nothing you wrote is silently lost. Shorten it and declare it again.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing stands in this theme at that document or passage: it was never placed or proposed there, or it has already been taken back. There is nothing to withdraw.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Taking a document or a passage out of a theme, or turning down a proposal, is a member's own judgment, done in their name. A machine may propose a placement; it cannot take one back.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A membership is taken back by the member who placed it, or by an administrator. Any member may turn down a proposal, but another member's placement stands on their judgment until they withdraw it.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say why. A placement taken back or a proposal turned down keeps its reason beside it, so the next reader of the theme can see what was judged and on what ground.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A source shows a version in force only up to the day it was last retrieved, and the date given is later than that. Give that day or an earlier one, or capture the source again. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The date a version is known in force through is a day written YYYY-MM-DD, and not before the day the version came into force. This one is not. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A version known in force through a date is recorded with the passage of the source checked that day, a captured document you may see. None was named, or it is not held. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A tier is stated only on a legal option, and is 1, 2, 3 or undetermined. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: One step here says it comes after a step this sequence does not contain, so the order cannot be worked out. Name a step that exists, or leave the ordering off and let it stand on its own.
words.note: progressions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That is not an outside service this group can hold a key for. Nothing was changed.
words.note: credentials' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The plan's record cannot be extended in place. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A version read from two captures names two held captures of one address whose texts differ, and the version it supersedes. These are not that. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That is not the shape a capture identity has, so nothing was looked up. A capture is named by the sha256 of its bytes; this says the request was malformed rather than letting it read as a document the record does not hold.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That request did not say which document address to read the versions of. Versions are versions OF something, so it asks rather than answering for a document you did not name.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record holds no version of that document with those bytes. Rather than pick the closest-looking one and call it the version before this, it says so — naming the wrong predecessor is the defect this read was built to end.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A watch ends on a calendar day, today or later, or has no end date. That day could not be used. Nothing was changed.
words.note: monitoring's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A project's kinds of work are drawn from: reporting, fixing, legal, oversight, other. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

step {i} of {n}
civicsmith.org
Civicsmith's own website: what it is, a group's published work, the groups that chose to be listed, and how to start a group.
Create your Civicsmith group
Creates your group's Civicsmith in a Cloudflare account your group controls: what you need, a permanent short name, Cloudflare's permission, then your one-time password.
Update your group's Civicsmith
Updates your group's Civicsmith to the signed release chosen in Settings › Updates, and no other. Records, members and settings are kept.
Your group's page
Your group's own page: who it is, what it has published, how to hand it material and how it works, with members' sign-in beside it.
How we work, step by step
How your group works, in six short steps, for anyone: no account needed, nothing recorded.
Choose a new password
Choose a new password from the one-time reset link an administrator made for you.
Forgot your password
How to get back in without email: use one of your recovery codes, or ask an administrator for a one-time reset link.
Become your group's first administrator
The first administrator's setup: claim the installation, then name the group, choose its places and languages, and decide how members reach the assistant.
Who your group is
What kind of group yours is, what it focuses on and why it exists. It shapes how members are welcomed and locks nothing.
Your invitation
Your invitation to join a group. Choose your language, the name the group will know you by, and a password.
Your group's home
Your group's home, the nerve center: what needs you, what needs the group, every area at a glance, the projects and what changed since you last looked. Start here each day.
Members
Everyone in your group and what each may do. Administrators invite members, set what they may do, and see who holds the hosting account.
Security
Administrators only: how hard your group's Civicsmith is being tried, by kind and by hour, against its own usual. Counts only; nothing names who tried.
Your account
Your own settings: your handle, password, signing key, language and expertise.
The assistant
Whether and how the assistant serves you: on your group's key, your own Claude account, or not at all. Set your limit and suggestions here.
Places and offices
Administrators only: the places whose rules your group's Civicsmith follows (deadlines, holidays, offices, records laws), and the offices and seats your group deals with.
Recovery codes
Your own recovery codes, which let you set a new password if you lose yours. Each works once.
Your group
Administrators only: your group's name, website, languages, court notice, hosting account and bar.
Settings
Every setting in one list: yours first, then the group's.
More
The places the tabs below do not hold: projects, people and settings.
Updates
Administrators only: the release your group's Civicsmith runs, the release ready to install and what changes in it, and the choice: Update, Not now or Skip this version.
Your ties
Your own ties to people or organizations the group may look into. Only you and the administrators see this list.
Your notes
Your private notes. Only you can see them in your group; turn one into an observation, a hunch or a question when you choose.
Translations
The words members see, in your group's languages. Members given the grant translate them, the assistant drafts where it can, and protected words are checked twice.
Wizards
Step-by-step walk-throughs of the real screens. Civicsmith's own come with each release; your group can write its own or copy one and change the copy.
Projects
Every project you can see: its stage, who works on it, how busy it is, and when it last changed.
Themes
The group's themes: lenses that gather documents and passages, never evidence.
The Action dashboard
The Action area as a dashboard: clocks and whose move it is first, then what needs you, then every action.
A project's dashboard
One project as a dashboard: your next steps here, the project at a glance, its story so far, and its activity.
Can't open this
What you see when an address leads nowhere, when something isn't yours to see, or when your group's Civicsmith can't be reached.
Where else to go
What you see when what you need is not Civicsmith's work: the places your group's place lists for it, each with what it does, how to reach it and where that came from. Opening it records nothing.
Your queue
Your queue: everything waiting on you, in one list. To do needs your act, Noticed is something new nobody has judged, and Status tells you where something stands.
Find
Find what your group holds, or look outside for something it doesn't yet. Capture what you find into the record.
Add
Add something to the record: a document from its address, a file, or what you saw yourself, in your own words.
Held captures
Captures waiting for a member to vouch for them before they enter the record. Release them, or set them aside with a reason.
Archive
One captured archive and every file in it: which are filed and held for review beside it, which were already held, and which were not filed and why.
Opening a file
Before a file opens: whether it is low or high risk and why, its safe view, the checks it has had, and how a held file is released.
Document
One document as captured: its words by page, its copy's grade, its versions beside each other, the links it carries, the people and organizations it names, and what cites it. Cite from here.
Find in this

Look through a document, the documents you are holding together, or a project for people, money, dates, requirements or a word. Each result shows its passage; you record what matters with the usual act.
Project
A project: its questions, their strength against the project's bar, its members and its stage. Open a question or a plan from here.
AI for this project
Question
One question: what supports it and what cuts against it, its strength against the bar, and what would change the answer.
Ask
Ask in plain words, with the assistant, or find and count without it. Answers come only from what your group holds, and show where they looked.
The assistant panel
A question with the assistant beside it. It answers only from what your group holds and never concludes, signs or sends.
People
The people and organizations your group's record follows, those named in your projects first, each with how often the record names them. Your own members are under Settings › Members.
Person
A person the record follows: positions over time, what they decided and signed, each fact dated and cited.
Timeline
What happened, in order: the city's acts and your group's acts in two lanes, never mixed. Undated items are listed apart.
Money trail
A money trail: figures from budgets and reports, each with its stage and period, included or left out with a reason.
Calculation
A calculation shown with its method and inputs, each tied to the record and recomputed when an input changes.
Help: How a records request works
What the law requires of the office you ask for records, the faster request, and what the city's portal shows.
Help: How spot-checks work
A help page: one of Civicsmith's methods explained in plain words, opened from the screens where it is used.
Explore connections
Chains of connections between people, votes, contracts and payments, each step cited and graded. A chain is a lead until a member cites its documents.
Proceeding
A court case or legal proceeding: its parties, its register of filings, and orders with their reply dates.
How this date was worked out
One due date and how it was worked out: the law or commitment it comes from and how the days were counted.
Standard
A standard the city set itself, held from its document, that questions can test the city against.
Action plan
An action plan: the options for what to do about a problem, the order to try them, and what each waits on.
Start and send
Start an option from a plan: prepare what is sent, check who it goes to today, and send it after the warning.
Request records
Ask an office for records under the law that requires it to answer. The due date is worked out for you.
Action
One action your group took: what was sent, to whom, when a reply is due, and what came back.
Matter
A matter: what the group is pursuing about one problem, from the first letter to the outcome.
Case
Prepare a case for publishing: its scope, statement, findings, the people it names and why, its timeline and what it leaves out.
Review copy
A draft case shared with named outside readers before publishing. Their comments come back here.
Publication ceremony
The publication ceremony: the last checks, then signing. Publishing is permanent; corrections come as a new edition.
A review copy, from outside
What someone outside the group sees when asked to review a draft case: the draft and a place to comment.
Published case
A case your group published, as anyone reads it: findings, their strength, the evidence, and how to check it without the group.
Another group's case
Another group's published case, recreated here. Nothing in it counts for your group until a member accepts it with a reason.
Docket
The public record of every edition, correction and withdrawal of your group's cases.
Inbox
Material handed to your group through its doorbell. Move it into the record, or discard it with a reason.
Hand material to the group
Hand material to the group. You need no account; the page says what will happen to what you send.

Takes you to Cloudflare's own page to allow this installer into your account, then sets up your group's Civicsmith there under your short name, or updates it. The short name is permanent: it appears in every address and beside every signature.
Signs you in on this device with your handle and password, for as long as you chose. Several wrong tries pause sign-in from here for a while.
Unlocks this device with your password after it locked while you were away, and takes you back to where you were; nothing was lost. A wrong password counts as a refused sign-in.
Sets a new password with one of your recovery codes, for any member. The code is spent, and every other sign-in of yours ends.
Sets the languages your group's members use: Civicsmith's own words are shown in each, and members choose among them when they join. The places whose rules apply are not changed.
Replaces the logo shown beside your group's name on its page, its masthead and its published cases. A logo is optional; with none, the name stands alone.
Sets your new password from the reset link an administrator made for you. The link is spent, every other sign-in of yours ends, and your handle and work stay as they are.
Signs you out on this device. Your work stays in your group's Civicsmith.
Signs you out on every phone and computer you are signed in on, this one included.
Starts joining through the group's join link: the name the group will know you by, then your handle and password.
Makes a one-time link for this member to choose a new password, valid for seven days. You send it yourself; Civicsmith sends no email. Their other sign-ins end when they use it.

Lists the people and organizations your group's record follows: each with its role or office, how many documents, questions and projects name it and when the newest was added, those your projects touch first. A read: it changes nothing.
Makes you the group's first administrator, using the one-time password from installing. Until it is claimed, nobody can use the group's Civicsmith.
Sets the name members and readers see. It can be changed later; the short name cannot.
Proves your group controls this web address, so published cases can show it as yours.
Chooses the places whose rules apply (deadlines, records laws, holidays) and the group's languages. Deadlines and wizards draw on these.
Lists the public offices and seats for your places, so requests and people can be addressed by role.
Adds something the record does not hold yet, such as an office, an organization or a court case, with a note on where it comes from.
Names a place Civicsmith does not yet hold rules for. Administrators are told when an update brings it.

Keeps the group's material away from AI, for every use or the ones you choose. It binds every account, the group's, any project's and members' own. Members see your reason on Settings › The assistant.
Holds one Anthropic API key for the group, sealed and never shown again. It pays for a member's act when neither a project's account nor the member's own serves it.
Turns the group's key on or off without removing it. Members who rely on it are told what changed.
Chooses whether members are told, when they join and the first time they record something not public, what a court order could reach.
Records who holds the Cloudflare account. Whoever holds it can reach everything, so the group should know who that is.
Opens the installer's update page for your group, set to the release you chose and no other. Nothing changes until whoever holds the group's Cloudflare account allows it there.
Puts this release aside for every administrator. It comes back later, the next day for a security fix, and at once when a newer release replaces it.
Says your group will not install this release, with your reason kept on the record for every administrator to see. The next release is offered as usual.
Adds a security tool your organization uses. Before it is turned on you see what it is sent, who receives it and how long it keeps files.
Creates an invitation for one person, under the cover the group knows them by. Nothing about them is public.
Saves what your group is, what it focuses on and why, and who may see each part: members only, or also the public.
Asks the assistant for a draft of your group's description, labeled as its draft. Nothing is saved until you keep it.
Shows who invited you, to which group, and what joining means, before you decide.
Sets the language Civicsmith speaks to you. Documents stay in their own language.
Joins the group with a handle and password. Your handle is how members see you; it need not be your name.
Starts from where you are: a problem you live with, a document, a deadline, a claim to check or a person. Each opens the right first step.
Changes what a member may do: contribute, administer. The change is recorded with who made it.
Changes a member's status, for example to inactive. Their past work stays in the record under their handle.
Adds your endorsement to make a member an administrator. With one administrator the group depends on one person.
Removes an administrator's powers, with a reason. It cannot leave the group with none.
Confirms a member's declared expertise, so it can be asked for when a check needs it.
Cancels an invitation nobody has used yet. The link stops working at once.
Creates a key that lets your group's website invite people, through an open form or an application someone approves.
Turns on one reusable link anyone with it can use to ask to join. You can turn it off at any time.
Removes the group's key for good. Members without their own account use Civicsmith without the assistant.
Shows how hard your group's Civicsmith was tried over the period you choose, against its usual. Counts only.
Sends a harmless test file or address to the tool and shows its answer, so you know it works before relying on it.
Stops using this tool. Notes it already wrote stay on the files they concern.
Says what you know professionally, such as accounting or law. An administrator confirms it; members can then ask you for checks.
Changes your password. Every other session signed in as you ends, so anyone using an old one must sign in again with the new password.
Tells the project's owners, in their queues, that this edition is prepared and ready to sign. It signs nothing.
Withdraws a member's signing key, for a lost or stolen device. It stops working at once; what it already signed can still be checked.
Makes your signing key in this browser and registers its public half with your group, so readers can check what you sign. Civicsmith never sees the key.
Withdraws your signing key, for example if it was lost. Cases already signed keep a record that it was withdrawn.
Chooses how quickly explanations open: promptly, or guidance on a longer pause so less opens while you move. Nothing is ever hidden.
Confirms you have read that your questions go to Anthropic under the group's account. Asked once, before your first question.
Confirms you have read what connecting your own account means: your questions go to Anthropic under your own account and terms.
Opens Anthropic's own sign-in page in a new tab, then connects your subscription with the code it gives you. Civicsmith never sees your password, and the code is used once and never kept.
Disconnects your Claude subscription from your group's Civicsmith. The group's key serves you instead, if the group has one.
Connects your own Claude API key. It serves only you, before the group's key, and Anthropic bills you for each use.
Disconnects your own API key and removes it from your group's Civicsmith. The group's key serves you instead, if the group has one.
Lists a tie that could matter to a case: an employer, a relative in a public body, a business interest. A case that concerns it says so.
Removes a tie from your list. A case already published keeps what it said.
Writes a note only you can see. Use it for thoughts not ready for the group.
Turns your note into something the group shares: an observation, a hunch or a question. The note itself stays private.
Changes your note. Notes are yours alone, so nothing else changes.
Deletes your note. If you turned it into something shared, that stays.
Asks the assistant to help word what you are writing, from what you typed. Its words arrive labeled as its draft; nothing is saved until you keep them.
Asks the assistant to draft translations of Civicsmith's words, labeled as drafts for a speaker to check.
Keeps a translation so members reading that language see it. Protected words need a second speaker's check first.
Lets a named member translate Civicsmith's words into one language.
Confirms a protected word as a second speaker, so members see it instead of the English.
Undoes a translation change in one step, back to what it replaced.
Shows the wizards your group can use: Civicsmith's, and those your group wrote.
Records a new wizard by walking through the steps yourself. It stays a draft until approved.
Changes a draft wizard's steps or words before it is submitted.
Submits a draft wizard for an administrator to approve before members are offered it.
Approves a wizard so members are offered it where its steps start.
Stops offering a wizard. Anyone part-way through can finish.
Does what this item asks, on the screen it concerns. It leaves your queue when done.
Passes this item to another member better placed to act, with a note.
Dismisses a suggestion or hint with a reason, kept on the record so the same thing is not raised again without cause.
Hides the item until the date you choose, when it comes back.
Stops this kind of item, or a project's items, reaching your queue. What you muted is listed under Muted at the foot of your queue, where you can turn each back on.
Moves your citations to the newer version of this document. You see what changed first.
Keeps citing the version you cited. The newer one stays in the record beside it.
Answers a reminder you set, for example that a reply came or a deadline passed.
Opens a question the group will answer with the record, from this hint, chain or suggestion. The source is kept with it.
Searches everything your group holds that you may see: documents, passages, questions, people.
Holds the items you picked together so one act can apply to them all. The set is held until the time shown.
Looks inside these documents for people, money figures, dates, requirements or a word. Each result shows its passage; nothing is recorded until you record it.
Lets the held set go. Nothing in it changes.
Shows where nobody has looked yet for this, so the group knows what an answer does not cover.
Has your group's Civicsmith fetch this address itself and keep exactly what the site sent, with when and from where.
Adds this file or photo to the record, with who made or obtained it and how. It waits in Held captures until vouched for.
Records what you saw or heard yourself as testimony: grade D, labeled as yours, never changed afterwards.
Asks for this to be captured later, for example when a site is down. The request waits until it can be fetched.
Checks this address once, now, for a new version. A new version is kept beside the old. To keep checking, turn watching on.
Gives you ten new one-time recovery codes for your own role, shown to you once, and spends every earlier unused one. Nobody else can see or use them.
Turns watching on or off for this document's address, and sets how often it is checked. Each new version found is kept beside the old, and you are told.
Shows captures waiting for a member to vouch for them before they count.
Vouches that each copy is what its source gave, unaltered. It is signed with your name; it can be corrected later, never silently undone.
Sets the picked captures aside with one reason, shown to anyone waiting on them. They can be restored.
Brings a set-aside capture back, with a reason, so it can be vouched for.
Explains this copy's grade: how it was obtained and what would raise it.
Lists the archive's files by state: filed, already held, or not filed and why.
Opens the original file on your device. A low-risk file is checked first if its last check is over a week old.
Opens a high-risk original on your own device without a deeper check, after you confirm you will not enable macros or editing.
Shows a safe copy: each page as a picture, or a spreadsheet's figures as data. Nothing in it can run. Cite the original, not this.
Runs every check on this file: read whole, the built-in scanner again, and your group's outside tools. A clean result opens the original to everyone for 24 hours.
Gives your reason to release a file a scanner flagged. A second member's reason releases it; the machine never can.
Cites this passage in a question, as support or as cutting against it. A citation always points at the original document.
Adds a name documents use for them, or takes one off with your reason. Civicsmith then looks for the name in the documents your group holds; a shared name never decides which one a document means.
Declares a tie between two people or organizations the record follows, with why and where it is said. It reads “declared, not evidenced” until a source that states it is attached.
Has Civicsmith match this document's mention to them, by an identifier or the name, and grade the match. A stronger match raises the grade; a match never falls.
Records from your own knowledge that this mention is them, with how you know. It is your word, grade D: never established on its own, and never lowering a stronger match.
Joins the documents that name them, pair by pair, each connection graded by the weaker of the two matches. Civicsmith also does this on its own as documents arrive.
Asks the assistant for options on this plan. It opens one planning run; the options it finds wait in the tray, labeled as its work, until a member adopts one. Nothing in the plan changes by asking.
Backs a step someone declared with a passage of a document your group holds that states it. The step then rests on evidence, graded like the document it cites.
Takes back a source you attached to a declared step, with your reason. The step goes back to resting on someone's word, and the earlier source stays in its history.
Records that a reply asks not to be quoted, in the reply's own words, or takes that record back. The case can still say what the reply says, never in its words.
Shows this passage in the language you read, as machine work, with the original one tap away. Nothing is saved, and the original is never replaced.
Shows the proceeding's own dates and your group's deadlines on it, as two lanes side by side. It says when things are due; it never says anyone is late.
Shows administrators the release your group runs, when it last checked for a new one, and any release ready to install, with its notes.
Shows how much of the assistant an account has used, day by day, against each of its limits, to the people who pay for it.
Draws what the record joins to one person, organization or document, two steps out, with how strong each connection is.
Lists the standards proposed in this project and what became of each: adopted, set aside, or still open.
Shows a prepared text exactly as it was saved, so leaving the page between preparing and approving loses nothing.
Shows the pressure your group has put on an action or project: what was done, when, and what came of it.
Remembers when you last looked at Home, so Home can show what happened since.

Records what the group has at stake in this project beyond its usual stake. It goes beside the group's statement on what this project sends or publishes, dated and attributed; clearing it leaves the group's statement alone.

Records what the group has at stake in this one action beyond its usual stake and the project's. It goes beside them on what the action sends, dated and attributed; clearing it falls back to the project's stake.
Sets the handle you sign in with from now on, once: the name the record shows on your work. Until you choose, you sign in as admin.

Switches the project between hidden (only its members know it exists) and findable (every member of the group sees it in Projects and can ask to join), with a reason kept in its history. Only an owner changes it.
Makes a member an owner. With one owner, that owner decides alone; with two or more, every owner agrees, each by making the same change.
Ends someone's ownership, with a reason; they stay a member. A project always keeps at least one owner, and with three or more owners the others agree first.
Takes a member off the project, with a reason they see. Their work on it stays, under their name.
Tells the owners you are leaving the project, with a note if you like. An owner can leave once another owner remains.
Starts a new project of your own from this one, with you as its only owner and the visibility you choose.
Makes an administrator an owner of a project whose owners are all gone, with a reason on its record. Never for a project a member kept for themselves alone.
Puts what you picked on your watch list: Find shows it under Watched by you, and a change to it reaches your queue. Only you see what you watch.
Asks the group to look at what you picked again, with a note saying why. It shows under Flagged for a second look until a member clears the flag.
Sets how carefully the group should act on this, from 1 (file freely) to 3 (do not file without counsel), with a reason kept in its history. Only a member sets it.
Puts a law beside the one chosen, for a member to weigh. It changes nothing until a member chooses it.
Opens a question with this action carried as its reference. You write the question; the action is where it comes from, not evidence in it.

Records, for each passage this question cites, whether your answer falls if that passage turns out wrong, or still holds because of other passages you cite. Civicsmith works the strength out from these answers. Once the strength has been shown, a change needs a reason, and the strength before and after is kept beside it.
Accepts this reading as a sound account of what supports the question. A project can then stand on it. Recorded with your name and the date.
Hides this reading from the list. Nothing is deleted: it stays on the record, and anyone can show the hidden readings again.
Marks this reading as one the group is weighing, with a reason. It is not yet accepted, so no project can stand on it.
Rejects this reading, with a reason. It stays on the record, rejected, and can be weighed again later.
Takes back the last decision on this reading, with a reason, so it is weighed again.
Makes this accepted reading the one the project stands on, with a reason. The question does not change; only the project's choice does, and the earlier choice stays on the record.

Picks which mention of them on this page the record reads as the one that connects them: where they are named on the point that matters. Until a member chooses, Civicsmith takes the strongest-graded mention. Your choice is dated and attributed; a later choice replaces it.
Stops using this copy in new work, with a reason. Questions that cite it are told.
Has an independent timestamp service certify that this exact copy existed by now: a timestamp over its fingerprint. It adds no signature of yours and says nothing about whether the copy is true.

Says this name refers to a person the record already follows, with how sure you are (a grade) and why. It is shown as a claim, "claimed the same person, grade B, because…"; the records are linked, never merged, and anyone can see the reason or withdraw it with theirs.
Keeps asking this as new documents arrive; new matches reach your queue once, as a list.
Records a fact about this person from the passage: a position, a credential, an interest. It cites the passage.
Records a dated fact from the passage, citing it, for the timeline.
Works out a due date from the law and the dates, showing each day counted and each holiday skipped. It proposes the date; a member confirms it.

Switches one use on or off for this account: asking, drafting, runs, standing questions, suggestions, or exploring (No, Ask every day, Yes). An act this account would pay for, with its use off, stops; it never moves to another account.
Sets or removes one limit on this account: overall, for one use, or for each member's use, in dollars (estimated, API keys only), tokens or calls, a day or a month. It binds this account only.
Holds an Anthropic API key for this project, sealed and never shown again. Switched on, it pays for members' acts in the project, before their own accounts or the group's key.
Makes your own Claude sign-in the project's account, allowed only while you are its only member. If another member joins, it stops serving the project at once and you are told.
Turns the project's account on or off without removing it. While it is off, members' own accounts, then the group's key, serve in the project.
Removes the project's account. Members' own accounts, then the group's key, serve in the project from then on.
Records that you have read what the project's key means, before the first act it pays for.
Keeps this project's material away from AI, for every use or the ones you choose, with a reason every member sees. It binds every account, whoever pays.

Makes this project a counsel matter, your own project, or neither, with your reason. A counsel matter's correspondence and dates are seen only by its members and never published; your own project is hidden and yours alone.
Chooses which acts in this project need a second member's approval before they are sent: a kind of action, a tier, or anything addressed to the public. Your reason is kept with the setting.
Drafts a rule of your group's own, a deadline or a legal fact, from the captured document that states it. It applies only after another member confirms it.
Confirms a rule another member drafted, after checking it against its source. For a Tier 2 or Tier 3 matter you state your professional qualification.
Withdraws one of your group's own rules, with your reason. It is kept, and no longer applied.
Gives you the rule, its source and its confirmation as one exact file, to send to whoever keeps your places' shared rules.
Proposes an obligation from the body's own reply or report: a promise it made, or a response the report requires, quoting it. A member adopts it before it is tracked.
Lists the obligations adopted from these documents, and whether each is met.
Shows the routes your places' rules and your group give for this kind of action, each with the law or rule it cites. Legal information, not legal advice.
Changes when your standing question stops being asked again.
Records, in your group's own words, what it stands to gain or lose. It is shown beside your group's name wherever its work is published.
Lists the dates proposed for this action's clock that no member has adopted yet: each with its rule, its basis and who or what proposed it. Adopting one is a separate act.
Shows administrators how the website key and the join link are set, and every change to them, with who made it and when. Never the key or the link itself.
Asks the assistant to point out sentences that read as a claim of breach, a policy position, an ask for your group, or naming staff. It never rewrites them; you decide.
Asks the assistant to draft a documentation of what happened from the record, labeled as its draft until you make it yours.
Asks the assistant to propose how the reply bears on each claim, labeled as its proposal until you lay it out yourself.
Runs every publication check on this case and holds it, checked and unsigned, until it is signed. Nothing is published.
Shows whether this case's check still holds, and if not, why.
Checks your own text, sentence by sentence, against the record: supported, not supported, or contradicted. Only in your own project, and only you see it.
Links a later act of the same office, found compliant, as what corrected an act found noncompliant. Undoing the link needs a reason.
Records a success in your own words: what changed and when, what shows it, figures computed from the record, and the order of events or a cause you can show.
Puts an outcome (a success, a correction by the office, or a harm addressed) into the case's next edition. It is published when that edition is signed.
Records that what you sent was received by them, or served on them, how and when. A deadline may count from it.
Makes this action confidential, or not, with your reason. A confidential action is seen inside the group and never published; the change applies to what is published from now on.
Records a promise your group made to a person, such as an embargo or anonymity, or ends one.
Lists your group's other open actions with the same office. It is information, never a block.
Lays out the reply claim by claim: for each, whether it brings new evidence, disputes without evidence, or doesn't address it.
Proposes a claim-by-claim layout of the reply, labeled as a proposal and kept apart until a member lays it out.
Records that a project or a matter in a plan arose from this reply.
Records pressure that arrived outside any action, such as a letter, post or call. A legal threat can carry a litigation hold.
Records that you sent the litigation hold notice, with a copy or your account of how.
Records that a partner organization approved the same text in its own copy. Their copy must match word for word.
Gives the second approval this project requires before sending. Only a member other than the first approver can give it.
Stops pursuing this escalation, with your reason. It is never recorded as ended or as a success, and it can be reopened where it stopped.
Asks the assistant for a first draft of this status report from the plan's items. The draft is labeled machine work, each line cites what it rests on, and nothing is saved until you save it as yours.
Starts a run on your own Claude sign-in, for you alone: checking this, or planning how to look into it. What it produces is labeled machine work and changes nothing until a member acts on it.
Reopens an escalation your group stopped pursuing, at the stage where it stopped, with your reason.
Sets this scenario aside, with your reason. It is kept whole, and can be restored.
Brings a set-aside scenario back, with your reason.
Pauses this plan, with your reason and, if you like, a day to look at it again. What it set running carries on.
Resumes a paused plan, with your reason.
Records, in your group's own words, the outcome it wants for this matter.
Takes this item's to-dos for yourself. Nobody assigns anybody; you choose.
Records that this plan set this watch running, so the plan knows to ask whether to keep it when it closes.
Keeps this watch until a date you choose, or stops it now.
Sets or removes the date to stop following this.

Has the assistant read up to 8 pages of this document that Civicsmith's own reading couldn't make out. The account that pays for your acts here pays, within its limits. Types the words of a page yourself, from its image. Your typing is labeled as yours, and a second member can check it against the page.
Lets the assistant explore today, on this account, what it said is worth exploring. Without a yes today, it doesn't.

Changes the handle the record shows on your work. Members see your earlier handle beside it, and no one else can ever take it. Allowed until your work first appears in a published case; after that it is fixed.

Holds this requirement as a standard the city set itself, so questions can test the city against it.
Reads this figure into a money fact, with its stage and period, citing where it came from.
Says what a table's columns are, so its figures can be counted through a calculation rather than one by one.
Sets the group's bar: how strong an answer must be before the group relies on it, in every project that sets no bar of its own.

Sets this project's own bar, with your reason: the strength each of its questions is measured against. It never changes the group's bar and holds nothing back; it shows how far each answer is from the bar.
Brings a question from elsewhere in your group into this project, with a note on why. The project draws on it; the question stays where it is, and is not copied.
Ties what you recorded at one drawn report to the spot-check: repaired, not repaired, or could not tell. It counts toward the estimate only for a report in the draw.

Lists the projects you may see.

Checks your password, then does what you asked, once. Nothing else changes.

Removes this citation from the question, with the reason kept. It can be reinstated.
Puts a removed citation back on the question.
Narrows the question to what the record can answer, with the reason. The wider question is kept.

Withdraws the question's answer, with a reason, for example after new evidence.
Keeps a hunch beside the question, labeled as yours. A hunch is never evidence and never moves an answer.
Shows one matter followed through a progression: each step in order with the documents threaded to it, how sure the chain is, and any finding.
Shows a progression: its steps, what each needs before it, how soon, whether it is required, its basis, and every version.
Declares a progression, or a new version of one: its steps and their basis. A revision needs a citation; the old version stays.
Places a document the group holds on a step of a matter it concerns, with the document's own date. Each threading is a new version, so nothing is overwritten.
Records why a required step was lawfully skipped: the document that shows it, your reason and the citation. The finding then reads as a lawful skip.
Shows every step of every matter this document is threaded to, with any finding there.
Lists the group's themes, newest first, or what one theme gathers: what was placed in it, then its hunches apart. Documents you cannot open are left out.
